Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the proceedings of today's National Assembly meeting will commence at (12:20 PM). Time has been requested by honorable members to speak during the urgent time. I have set a time limit of a maximum of 3 minutes for speaking during the urgent time. I will now provide time to the honorable members sequentially. First, Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.
Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, when the first meeting of the Federal Parliament was held on May 10th, during the reading of the Government of Nepal's annual policy and program by the Right Honorable President, we witnessed an unprecedented, unparliamentary, immature, impolite, and undignified behavior for the first time in Nepal's history. All democratic forces and citizens of Nepal are saddened. We feel that such impolite behavior is a major attack on democracy. Therefore, Honorable Chairperson, today there is a program to discuss the policy and program presented by the government. But when such undemocratic and undignified behaviors continue to occur (.. sound not audible).
Honorable Chairperson, if the honorable members of the Federal Parliament disregard the annual policy and program presented by the Right Honorable President on behalf of the Government of Nepal as if it were the Right Honorable President's personal program, how can parliamentary practice and parliamentary culture be maintained? Therefore, I want to convey to the Government of Nepal through the Honorable Chairperson that such unparliamentary behavior can no longer be tolerated. Therefore, I strongly demand that the Right Honorable Prime Minister come to the house and provide information about what happened. And regarding the discussion on the Government of Nepal's policy and program, which is on the agenda today, if the honorable members do not take ownership of this discussion and this policy and program, the question arises whether to discuss it or not. Therefore, I request the Honorable Chairperson to provide information to the house about this. I request that this be clarified by the Right Honorable Chairperson in the house. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.
Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable Chairperson, regarding the policy and program presented by the Right Honorable Prime Minister Mr. Bal Krishna Khand in the joint meeting of the Federal Parliament held on the 28th, unfortunately, it was unprecedented in the sense that it had never happened before. Similarly, it was a novel event that during the reading of the policy and program by the Right Honorable President, there was an absence. Regarding this absence, I agree with what the honorable member who spoke just before said. While agreeing, I want to say that such an incident has definitely never happened in Parliament before. That's why I called it unprecedented earlier. What was the reason for this absence? We want to demand it. Although his secretariat stated it was due to health reasons, if it was due to health reasons, what kind of health is it? Was he unwell while the President was addressing, and then recovered after the address? What kind of health is it? If it was due to his inexperience or immaturity, it might be forgivable. But what is it? Why did that incident happen? Why was it done? We want to know about this.
Honorable Chairperson, we saw it on the screen during the meeting. We thought perhaps he had come for some reason, but that did not happen. Therefore, if this is an insult to the Right Honorable President, we definitely cannot tolerate it. But what is the real reason? The Right Honorable Prime Minister must come to the house and provide a clear explanation. Because if the Right Honorable Prime Minister himself is absent while the Right Honorable President is reading the address presented by him, it is not a trivial matter. If he had other engagements, he could have adjusted them according to his convenience. If there was any other reason, I do not want to raise questions about his intentions here. Because he has broken a sequence in history. There have been 40/42 Prime Ministers in Nepal's history so far. No person from the oppressed Madhesi community has ever been Prime Minister. Therefore, we do not want to question his intentions now, nor do we want to criticize him. But why did this unprecedented event happen in history? This honorable house has the right to know. Therefore, I also want to state that the Right Honorable Prime Minister must come and provide a clear explanation. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe.
Honorable Mr. Roshni Mechhe (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, while the Government of Nepal was presenting the policy and program for the fiscal year 2026/2027 on May 10, 2026, and all honorable members were listening seriously to the policy and program being presented by the Right Honorable President, our Right Honorable Prime Minister got up and left in the middle. This has seriously drawn our attention. Because Parliament is a place where all honorable members present the voice of the people in an organized and dignified manner. Another thing is that we showed such undignified and disorganized behavior in front of the Right Honorable President. This is the first time such an incident has happened in the history of Nepal. Therefore, through Parliament, I want to draw the serious attention of the Honorable Chairperson. The Right Honorable Prime Minister must come to the house and answer for such undignified behavior. I also urge the Right Honorable Prime Minister to be present in the house to provide this answer. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, we have taken serious note of the issue raised by the honorable member here. We will discuss it in the secretariat and proceed. I have said this much to the honorable members for now.
Honorable members, the order of speaking by honorable members during the urgent time concludes here. Honorable members, names of honorable members have been received to speak during the zero hour. I will provide time to the honorable members to speak. I have set a time limit of one minute for each honorable member to speak during the zero hour. First, Honorable Kamala Pant.
Honorable Mr. Kamala Pant (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, the Gorakhkali Rubber Industry, which was started with great enthusiasm and pride as a national pride project in 2049 BS (1992 AD), operated well until 2074 BS (2017 AD). After 2074 BS, the industry has not been in operation. This government, with a two-thirds majority, has expressed its commitment to operating sick industries. The Gorakhkali Rubber Industry, spread over two hundred ropanis of land on the banks of the beautiful Marsyangdi River, is an industry of national pride. Will this industry be operated, and from when will it be started? I want to know. Chairperson, thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.
Honorable Mr. Jayanti Devi Rai (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable Chairperson, as we all know, the government bulldozed the settlements of the landless without prior notice, without alternative arrangements, and without identification. Today, the condition of these landless people is extremely tragic compared to yesterday. Yesterday they were kept in hotels, but today they are being kept in various shelters, truly making them landless. There is no arrangement for living or eating. The children's schooling is disrupted, and their employment is lost. Their work is lost. Therefore, if we look at their bedding, they have no place to sleep, and the sick, the elderly are getting extremely sick. Therefore, they are given food twice a day, but children need to eat two or three times a day. Therefore, we have just seen their extremely pitiable condition. Therefore, I want to draw the serious attention of the government through the Honorable Chairperson and urge that alternative arrangements be made for them immediately. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Durga Gurung.
Honorable Mr. Durga Gurung (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, the government appears powerful when it bulldozes the houses and huts of the poor and landless. But why does it become weak when the bulldozer reaches in front of the houses and offices of those with political connections and leaders? Is the law in this country only for the poor? It is extremely sad and shameful that the landless are driven to suicide due to the pain of their houses being demolished. After all, is the government's ego greater than the lives of the people? Isn't it? I want a clear answer from the government. Who will take responsibility for the tears and deaths of the poor? When will landless people receive dignified arrangements instead of oppression? Does the government have a concrete plan with a timeline to solve the landless problem, or will it give false assurances to the public until the next election?
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Nar Bahadur Bisht.
Honorable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bisht (Nepal Communist Party):- Chairperson, Nirmala Basnyal died in Dubai, Surkhet Bheri Ganga Municipality Ward 10. Similarly, Devendra BC died in Malaysia. This government was formed to provide employment and came to power with a two-thirds majority. Within a month of forming the government, 62,000 people have gone to work in foreign lands, and people like Nirmala Basnyal committed suicide because she had a visa for Dubai. She went to Qatar on a Dubai visa and committed suicide because she couldn't stay there. It seems there was a tradition where brokers sold and distributed such people for up to 4 lakh rupees. Therefore, through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the attention of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. We need an answer for this. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra.
Honorable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, while praising all the good deeds of this government, demolishing the settlements of the landless and irregularly settled people without proper management and without even a 15-day notice is like mocking human rights and democracy. Furthermore, on August 24th, when historical documents in courts across the country, including the Supreme Court, turned to ashes and justice was thrown into disarray, the decision made in the name of the Constitutional Council has caused fear that a tradition of judicial proceedings being influenced by the executive might be established, contrary to the tradition and history of the courts, regarding the recommendation for the Chief Justice. If the court, which is the final referee of democracy, and the Supreme Court, which is repeatedly under scrutiny, is forced to operate within a strong circle of bias, will we be forced to live in fear that justice is disappearing from the country?

Government should also pay attention to the protection of democracy. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar.
(12:36 PM)
Honorable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable
(12:36 PM)
Chairperson, a citizen has been killed in the Khukot police custody in Sindhuli. An inter-caste love marriage led to a murder. In Surkhet, the student Inisa B.K. was murdered for Krishna Bishwakarma. In Rolpa, an innocent child was beaten severely, accused of being inside the house. Rastriya Swatantra Party, is the government dead for justice for the Dalit community? I demand an investigation into the incident and strict action. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable member Madan Kumari Shah Garima.
(12:36 PM)
Honorable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable
(12:37 PM)
Chairperson, while the policy and program for the fiscal year 2083/084 were being presented by the Honorable President in the joint session, the Honorable Prime Minister walked out in the middle. This act of his has insulted not only the Honorable President but also the entire house. What kind of civilization is it to walk out without voting on the motion of thanks to the President whom you yourself invited? What kind of culture is this? If there are rules inside the house, this is parliament. Parliament has established norms and values that everyone must respect. Through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to send a message to the Prime Minister: Parliament is not a place to play where you come wearing a "malchaato" and sports shoes. Let's not devalue parliament. Through the Honorable Chairperson, I want to tell the Prime Minister. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable member Yuvraj Sharma.
(12:38 PM)
Honorable Mr. Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, my clear
(12:38 PM)
view is that a broken pen cannot write history or biography. In a democracy, the minority is respected, but today the government seems to have chosen the path of ordinances without respecting its majority. It is unclear what kind of history of accountability is being created through the disrespect and silence of the head of government. It appears the government is proceeding in a dictatorial manner without focusing on structural reforms and institutional strengthening. It reminds one of Muhammad bin Tughluq, as described in Indian history. Therefore, there is more hope than despair. What citizens want is accountability. It is the solution to citizens' problems. More than that, it is democracy. This requires immense effort. Regarding good governance, remember that even Ram had to banish Sita. Finally, through the Chairperson, I urge the head of government to maintain the dignity and sanctity of parliament. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.
(12:39 PM)
Honorable Ms. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepal Communist Party):- Honorable Chairperson,
(12:39 PM)
Today is International Health Day. International Health Day, it has started this year. May we have such good weather that it does not affect anyone's health. I want to extend this wish, and speaking in relation to health, I want to talk about reproductive health. Today, a husband and wife from an educated family, a learned family, went to a clinic for an abortion. From one clinic to another, then to another, Gita Pandey died during her abortion. Her husband has protested, saying injustice has been done. This incident shows that the government still needs to pay attention to the health sector. I want to say that we should move forward sensitively in the health sector.
Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable member Sonam Geljen Sherpa.
(12:40 PM)
Honorable Mr. Sonam Geljen Sherpa (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable
(12:40 PM)
Chairperson, traffic rules are being strictly enforced across the country. This is a good thing. Because it reduces accidents and manages the roads better. However, while traffic rules are enforced on the general public outside, the way traffic rules are implemented inside Singha Durbar, the way vehicles are parked on the sidewalks, parked anywhere, parked in pedestrian areas, this is not good. Laws apply to the general public. No action is taken against anyone, from employees to leaders, inside Singha Durbar. This is not good. Therefore, I strongly demand that those who violate traffic rules inside Singha Durbar also be brought under the purview of action. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable members, the Zero Hour where honorable members speak

concludes here.
Honorable members, I now provide time to the Honorable Chairperson of the Legislative Management Committee, Krishna Bahadur Rokaya, to present the committee's report on the Intangible Cultural Heritage Protection Bill, 2081, to the house.
Honorable Chairperson of the Legislative Management Committee, Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya:-
(12:42 PM)
Honorable Chairperson, the meeting of the National Assembly held on Magh 14, 2082, sent the Intangible Cultural Heritage Protection Bill, 2081, originating in the National Assembly, to this committee. Twenty-three honorable members registered amendment proposals in seven groups, individually and jointly, on this bill. Amendment proposals were submitted on the preamble, the long title, and twelve articles, with fifty points in ten articles. Theoretical discussion on the bill along with the submitted amendment proposals was held on Magh 21, 2082, and discussions with stakeholders were held in the second meeting on the same day. Seven meetings of the committee were held based on the agenda of this bill. As Nepal became a party to the Convention on Intangible Cultural Heritage, 2003, in 2010, it has an obligation to protect and manage intangible cultural heritage as stipulated by the convention, and this bill has been introduced to give concrete form to that arrangement. The present bill provides for the identification and preparation of inventories of intangible cultural heritage by the three tiers of government, as well as grants the concerned communities the right to protect their heritage. Similarly, the bill provides for the declaration and listing of individuals who make significant contributions to the practice, protection, and promotion of intangible cultural heritage and its intergenerational transfer to the community as Living Human Treasures. The then Honorable Minister who presented the bill, the current Honorable Minister overseeing the relevant ministry, honorable members of the committee, honorable members who proposed amendments, relevant employees of the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, and relevant employees of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs were present in the committee meetings. In this bill of twelve articles, the committee has amended all articles except Article Ten and the preamble, thereby revising the bill. I express my sincere gratitude to all those who participated in the various formal and informal discussions on this bill and assisted in the report writing. 
Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Honorable Chairperson, I present to this esteemed house the committee's report on the Intangible Cultural Heritage Protection Bill, 2081, passed by the committee on Baishakh 15, 2083. Thank you.

Honorable members, regarding the policy and program of the Government of Nepal for the fiscal year 2083/084, 8 amendment proposals, including one joint amendment proposal from 19 honorable members, have been received. Honorable members proposing amendments must participate in the discussion along with their respective amendment proposals. It is also informed that time will be utilized on a party basis. Now I will provide time to honorable members to participate in the discussion sequentially. First, Honorable Member Kiran Babu Regmi. Time: 12 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Jhagendra Prasad Subedi.
Honorable Mr. Kiran Babu Regmi (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson,
(14:58 PM)
First of all, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the students who have passed the SEE examination, which is considered the iron gate for students in Nepal, and wish them a bright future. Honorable Speaker, it is a privilege to express my views on the policy and program for the fiscal year 2083/084 in this esteemed house today. On this occasion, I express my heartfelt respect for Nepal's democracy, constitution, the supremacy of the people, and the supremacy of parliament. We have waited for a long time, and although it is late, parliament has resumed today. Indeed, after much anticipation, like the pain of childbirth, I have finally received the opportunity to speak. And under our democracy, our constitution of 2072, the governance system in this country is being run under the Westminster Ministerial System, similar to that of the United Kingdom. This is not a model that has emerged from any philosophy or ideology. It is a style that has developed in the Palace of Westminster in London, and therefore, it is known as the Westminster Parliamentary System. Countries worldwide, following the UK as the mother of democracy, have been following this model. Similarly, Nepal, after the constitution of 2072, has implemented a federal democratic republican governance system under the parliamentary system, and by accepting the supremacy of parliament, we have realized that the welfare of all, the stability of democracy, and the future of Nepal lie in continuing as we have been doing and will do in the future. It has some fundamental principles. The parliamentary system, the Westminster system, has some fundamental principles, traditions, customs, practices, and culture. There are written...

The constitution does not exist. Although there is no written constitution, the customs, traditions, and practices of Britain have made its constitution and governance system very strong and more democratic, and have been taken as examples. Therefore, speaking in this assembly today, how much have we followed these parliamentary system practices, practices similar to Britain's, and the practices, behaviors, and customs of other countries in the parliamentary system? I think this is the most important issue today, and everyone needs to be serious about moving this forward. Only if everyone is serious will there be a future for Nepal, and I would like to draw attention to that. Honorable Chairperson, a new government was formed just a few months ago, one or one and a half months ago, and a debate has concluded. We have said many times standing on this rostrum, civil society has debated outside, and there have been debates within parties that this constitution cannot form a government that can secure a majority. Therefore, the constitution needs to be amended, we have said and debated many times, but that has not been resolved. The recently elected government has become a majority government, and it has actually proven that it is not a flaw in the constitution. It has been proven that a majority can be obtained even without amending the constitution. Although there may be some fundamental issues, history will evaluate them in the future. But the resolution of one issue is that this constitution was made by the people, by the parliament elected by the people, therefore the people themselves have decided it, and in the future, it has also been proven that the constitution is not an obstacle to moving this constitution forward. At the same time, the current government has brought up the issue of constitutional amendment in the current policy and program. Now, there is something to discuss here: is it constitutional amendment or constitutional reform? I think we need to keep this in mind for a while. What is constitutional reform? What is constitutional amendment? If the constitution is to be amended, every article needs to be changed, and it must be changed. If it is reform, we said in the 2036 referendum, didn't we, that we called it a reformed Panchayat system, not a constitution, but a reformed Panchayat system. Therefore, this issue will surely bring debate in the future. I also believe that the issue placed in the current policy and program will be discussed with consensus among all parties in the future, and the issues where the constitution has created obstacles will be moved forward. Also, after a new government was formed, some work has moved forward. It has moved at a rapid pace, and as decisions are made to move this work forward, some criticisms have been made and some support has been received. Criticism and support are not a big deal once a decision to work has been made. In this context, something comes to my mind. In 2015 BS, the Nepali Congress had secured a two-thirds majority, and they formed a very revolutionary government. At that time, BP Koirala was the Prime Minister, and he moved very revolutionary work forward. He talked about moving the country forward at a very fast pace, made decisions. And I had read somewhere that when Prime Minister Bishweshwor Prasad Koirala went to Burma, one of his socialist friends, leader Ne Win, had said, Prime Minister, you are riding a very fast horse, please remember that. Riding a fast horse has a high possibility of falling very soon. Now, somewhere, I feel that the current government, the current Prime Minister, is also riding such a fast horse, so please be careful. We, as the opposition party, will cooperate and support in moving the country forward and making it prosperous. But at the same time, if you do wrong, if this government does wrong, it is our role and duty as the opposition to alert you in the future and try to bring you back to the right path. As far as the policy and program presented by the government is concerned, I want to make some observations after studying it carefully. I think praise blinds the eyes, criticism hardens the heart. Observation shows the way to improvement with an open mind. It is not just about clapping and not just about the courage to point fingers, but also about trying to have an honest dialogue with the truth. In this context, I will try to present my thoughts and ideas. Looking at the presented policy and program as a whole, it is felt that it has not been able to be as planned, clear, credible, and result-oriented as the current economic and social situation of the country. Compared to the policy and programs of the past years 2081 BS and 2083 BS, there are many similarities with the current one. Some new things have been included in the initial pages, such as reformative decisions, and they are ambitious, and a little change is seen in that regard. Otherwise, I had heard a member of parliament say in the House of Representatives, "It seems like a verbatim copy of 2082 BS has been brought here, perhaps the person who wrote it is the same?" I also found many things repeated after a cursory look. Many things written in 2082 BS and 2081 BS, promises made, have been repeated in the current policy and program. Repeating promises is not new, and I don't consider it unusual. But, how many of those promises made yesterday were fulfilled? Why were they not fulfilled? Without reviewing that, when the same promises and the same programs are repeated, how successful will this be in the future? Will it just be a charade in the eyes of the people? These questions arise. Therefore, I hope that the current government will not just fill new wine in an old bottle, as the saying goes, because there are good things too. I also want to wish well that the current policy and program has followed the path shown by past governments and the good things promised, and it is good, and I don't think it should be considered otherwise. We all know that the country is facing serious economic challenges, industries are not operating at full capacity, youth are migrating abroad daily, the agricultural sector is in a disappointing state, market demand has decreased, and ordinary citizens are suffering from inflation. In such a situation, there was confidence that the policy and program brought by this government, which has a clear majority, would give hope, trust, and a clear direction to the people. However, the same old style and mostly old programs, just attractive slogans, and announcements with very good titles here and there have also been included. The realistic basis for implementation seems weak. Now, in the policy and program, the modernization, commercialization, and concessional loans in agriculture have been mentioned every year, which I have been saying for a long time. But concrete plans to bring about change in the lives of actual farmers are few, and farmers are forced to farm based on the weather due to lack of irrigation access. There are no sufficiently clear plans for irrigation, agricultural insurance, storage, processing, and market management. I also request that the tendency to prioritize agriculture in speeches and neglect it in budget and practice should not be repeated. Honorable Chairperson, now at the end, some things are missing here, the Budhigandaki Hydropower Project, and the issue of producing methane gas, natural gas in Jaljala, Dailekh, are not included in the policy and program. I request that they be included, and with that, I conclude my brief remarks. Thank you, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Jhakka Prasad Subedi, time 10 minutes. (15:11 hrs) Following this, Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dangal. Honorable Shri Jhakka Prasad Subedi (Nepal Communist Party): Honorable Chairperson (15:11 hrs) Sir, I would like to present my views regarding the government's policy and program, which was addressed by the Honorable President Ram Chandra Paudel in a joint session of both houses of the Federal Parliament. First of all, this policy and program is poetic and artistic. It is written with full artistry, and it is poetic in the sense that it is very enjoyable to read. But how much will it be implemented? I have put it later, I will call it poetic and artistic. The first issue is that after the Janjivan movement, the people had new expectations, and the new government also talked about a new brand. The people expected that the government would bring a systematic policy and program. But the policy and program came in the old format. As the previous honorable member also stated, there is no new economic policy, nor is there a new development model. There is nothing to focus on here, and it has not been able to clarify the direction. The first point emphasizes good governance. Good governance is written here with great emphasis, but looking at the government's work style for one month, implementation seems to be limited to paper only. There is nothing hopeful in this policy and program for the transformation of the country and the nation. It is not clear what will be the guiding principle in the policy and program. Neither the constitution is made the guiding principle, nor is SDG graduation mentioned anywhere. It has come saying that good governance is everything, borderless economy, weightless economy, this is just a slogan, as I said before, it is artistic and poetic. The policy and program are not based on facts. There is no analysis of our situation, no analysis of the country's situation, and the government has not been able to present where it will reach in five years from one or two years. Honorable Chairperson Sir, it has announced the launch of a new phase of economic reform with the goal of reaching an average economic growth rate of 7 percent in the coming decade. However, the 16th plan had already set this target of 7 percent economic growth. This is not new. There is no departure program in the policy and program for 7 percent economic growth. It has asked to reduce taxes for the elite class, but the poor and destitute are not on the government's radar. It has ignored the Tharus, Dalits, and marginalized communities. In one place, it talks about irrigation for Madhes, and nothing else. The destitute see nothing in the government's policy and program. After realizing that nothing can be achieved from a unitary system, a three-tiered government was brought in. Except for one point, it is not mentioned anywhere else. The constitution states that it is oriented towards socialism, democracy, republic, federalism, inclusivity, and the government's policy and program have bypassed the constitution. The policy and program emphasize most on making government services and the overall economy digital, but the issue of human resource production is limited to slogans. Point 18 says it will fix everything, why were bulldozers used on squatters? After identifying landless people and demolishing the huts of homeless squatters and devastating them, the issue of identifying landless people has come up. A program to identify landless people and ensure stability has come. Either this writing is wrong, or the bulldozing is wrong. One of the two is definitely wrong. The government has set a target of producing 30,000 megawatts of electricity in the coming decade in its program. We all know how the previous government managed to bring 10,000 megawatts. And the government is talking about 30,000 megawatts, Honorable Chairperson Sir, it is dreaming in broad daylight. Impossible things are also mentioned here. There is nothing radical in the policy and program regarding revenue collection. Because this policy this

This document is silent on the matter of national pride projects. The nation has made a huge investment in pride projects. There is no mention of the Nijgadh airport, nor of the Mid-Hill Highway. The Nijgadh airport has great significance, and it was indeed brought in as a game-changer plan for the nation. The education sector is not clear about its direction. Some issues are contradictory. On one hand, it says to make education up to secondary level free, but the government's policy and program is silent on enhancing the capacity of community public educational institutions and supplying skilled human resources. The state is not focused on increasing investment in education, but the policy and program seems to encourage the private sector, isn't that a contradiction? Another important issue here is that the current government, the party in power, Rastriya Swatantra Party, has greatly emphasized 100 points, it is in love with 100 points. It is in the election manifesto, it is in the government's agenda, it is in 100 points. This policy and program is also in 100 points. Not only that, it states in the policy and program that a minimum of 100 government services will be made available through the Citizen App. Regarding the government's 100 points, I have already mentioned the immense infatuation. Honorable Speaker, this policy and program is completely traditional, because the previous speaker started by emphasizing new things like good governance and economic matters. It has come up, but it doesn't mention how to collect revenue. But as we go further, it is written here that it is completely false. In point 60, it says to provide clean drinking water to everyone by 2087 BS. Currently, at most 25 percent of Nepali citizens have access to clean drinking water, and by 2087 BS, we will provide clean drinking water to 100 percent, this is good, but it is nothing more than entertainment for the public. Second, to transform foreign employment from a compulsion to an option, it has declared the decade from 2083 to 2093 BS as the Employment Promotion Decade, for 10 years. Is it possible for this government to implement this? It is absolutely impossible. The government seems to have no attention to this. Therefore, the former mayor of the metropolis had made efforts to manage waste as wealth. Is the current Prime Minister Balen or someone else? Honorable Chairperson, in many points of the policy and program, we have made efforts to go to Digital Nepal, but our technical expertise and human resources are not ready for Digital Nepal. The population with weak willpower and lack of capacity, who have certificates of authority and qualification, cannot deliver results. Therefore, the government must present a basis for its implementation. The policy and program is a partial improvement of the previous government's continuity. I request the current government to connect political achievements and opportunities with development and prosperity and to implement this policy and program with extensive reforms. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Durga Gurung, time 12 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar. Honorable Mr. Durga Gurung (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, on the 28th of this Baisakh, the Honorable President presented the policy and program of the Government of Nepal for the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084 in a joint meeting of the National Assembly and the House of Representatives. First of all, I extend my heartfelt thanks to the Honorable President. Honorable Chairperson, we are in a federal democratic republic. This system is a democratic system. This system has its own definite values and principles, which are established internationally and are continuously in practice. However, the style displayed in the parliament by the government of the political party that received a large mandate in the name of being new, was not understandable. Furthermore, the behavior of the Prime Minister while the President was presenting his own government's policy and program felt like a serious insult not only to the dignified sovereign parliament but also to the President, the highest institution of the country. I will not descend to the level of making curses like Honorable Mahabir Pun on social media, saying 'may you go to hell,' but through you, Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the Prime Minister's attention to maintain the dignity of the parliament in the future and to give due respect to the President. Honorable Chairperson, it is felt that the policy and program for the fiscal year 2083/084 has seriously neglected Karnali Province. Karnali Province, which is the most backward in the country and deprived of basic infrastructure for development, is not effectively included in any priority of the policy and program. Karnali Province has been confined to assurances again. After all, until when will Karnali Province remain a second-class province in the eyes of the state, I want to draw the government's attention through you, Honorable Chairperson. Honorable Chairperson, I believe we all understand that the current government is a strong and stable government. The party that has a single-party government has MPs with a two-thirds majority in the House of Representatives. Such a strong government postponed the parliamentary session called by the President and hastily brought half a dozen ordinances. I also oppose that. This process disregarded the role of the people's elected representatives. It questioned the effectiveness of the MPs in their field of work. It raised questions about the constitutional provision regarding when ordinances should be brought and created an insult and distrust towards the MPs. This action by the government also raised the question of whether the government is being directed from somewhere, and it has created serious suspicion that an attempt is being made to establish a tradition of operating the state in an arbitrary and autocratic manner that weakens democracy. In my mind, there was also suspicion that perhaps this policy and program would also come through ordinances. But that did not happen. I want to convey through you, Honorable Chairperson, that the government should now come on track and move forward while maintaining the dignity and sanctity of the parliament. Honorable Chairperson, the new party and the new government seem to like the number 100 very much. The 100-day agenda, 100 governance reform plans, policy and program, all have come in 100 points. It is a very good thing if the number 100, in the sense of 1000, is successful. But in our parliamentary history, two-thirds and majority have been achieved. The Nepali Congress's two-thirds in 2015, the Nepali Congress's majority in 2048, the Maoists' majority in the first Constituent Assembly's direct elections, and the NCP's two-thirds in 2074 are historical examples. What happened when there was necessary cooperation between parties in their work? If this Rashtriya Swatantra Party's two-thirds also becomes like this, it will not be 100 percent successful. I also want to caution. Honorable Chairperson, does this new government truly want to advance the country, or does it want to consolidate the achievements like republic and federalism brought by the people's great sacrifices and struggles under the guise of newness and move the country towards prosperity, or does it want to create a suitable environment for domestic and foreign forces that want to fish in troubled waters by pushing the country backward in the name of amending the constitution drafted by the Constituent Assembly, creating instability and conflict again? Through you, Honorable Chairperson, I want to ask the government: is the current need constitutional amendment or the transformation of the people's condition? The people are looking for employment. They are looking for prosperity and development, fair results, and newness. Therefore, I suggest to the government that the government's priority should be on these issues. Honorable Chairperson, although the 100-point policy and program presented by the government has some new words, it does not seem to have brought much newness. The political parties accused of being old, which were sought to be organized, played a very important historical role in bringing this system through long struggles, sacrifices, and martyrdom. The governments of those very parties...

This has come in continuation of the policy and program presented in the parliament. Some things are even abstract. I hope the policy and program will have the courage to respect the trust and support the public has given us through their votes. Whatever is new has come in the opposite direction. The policy and program have taken away the trade union rights of professionals. This is not appropriate. I would like to demand through you, Mr. Chairman, that this be removed from the policy and program: that the system be multi-party, but one cannot open organizations and talk about their rights. Honorable Chairman, the government has created a bulldozer terror for a large segment of the public at the basic level. The slum dwellers' settlements were removed in a cruel and inhumane manner without any proper and just management alternatives. As a result, the slum dwellers are in protest. It is unacceptable under any circumstances that ministers, MPs, and party leaders can do whatever they want, but the general public is in dire straits. The issue of managing slum dwellers also did not come in a concrete and tangible manner in the policy and program as it should have. First, guarantee the public's food, shelter, clothing, and employment, and then beauty. I also want to ask the government this question: who are the people living on the riverbanks? The government's goal of maintaining zero tolerance against corruption, improving public service delivery, and moving forward as a campaign for economic recovery and social progress is correct. However, if the government moves forward with political prejudice and vindictiveness, it will be a great misfortune for the country. I want to urge the government not to proceed in this manner. Honorable Chairman, I am not saying that the policy and program presented by the government to the parliament is entirely correct. Many correct things have also come up. We have a problem where we say things are correct, but they are never implemented accordingly in practice. I hope the government, ministers, and state mechanisms are freed from this disease. May the upcoming fiscal year's budget, based on this policy and program, come with a commitment and concrete plan to move towards self-reliance. May it come with a plan to end unemployment. May it come with a fair distribution of development and prosperity. May it come with solutions to the specific problems of the nation and the expectations of the people. Thank you, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairman: Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar, time 7 minutes. (4:24 PM) After this, Honorable Member Somnath Poudel. Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party): Honorable Chairman, I want to express my views on the policy and program of the Government of Nepal, which was presented by the Honorable Prime Minister in the joint meeting of the House of Representatives and the National Assembly on the 28th of Bhadra, but unfortunately, surprisingly, and unprecedentedly, in his absence. I am saying unprecedentedly not in the sense of "Wow, what a thing." Unfortunately, surprisingly, and unprecedentedly, in his absence, I want to express my views on the policy and program of the Government of Nepal, which was read by the President. Time is short, so I will go through it quickly. Looking at this policy and program superficially, I felt that this government has brought many new things, but the policy and program are a continuation of the old. The policies formulated by previous governments are also seen in this government. There is no reason to shift. There is no change in governance. This policy and program are not like the Gen Z movement that was rumored outside. It has not come accordingly. This program lacks focus. It lacks a destination. It is directionless. This policy and program do not adhere to the constitution. Achievements like federalism, republic, and inclusivity were great achievements, historical achievements. It does not build upon them and appears to be influenced by populism. This current government has talked a lot about youth. But this policy and program are not for youth. Therefore, friends, "You are betrayed" by the youth, and this policy and program, at the beginning of this policy and program, it is mentioned that there was participation of the youth generation on the 23rd and 24th of Bhadra. If this is the case, then this government is also responsible for the activities that took place on the 24th. The movement on the 23rd was a just and legitimate agenda by Gen Z; I salute that just and legitimate movement. But was the movement on the 24th a movement? Destruction happened on the 24th. Government structures were burning fiercely, and all of them were burnt and destroyed. Were these criminal activities a movement? This government is also responsible for that. I think this needs to be separated. The immediate Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli's oppression was the reason for the reaction on the 23rd, but who is responsible for the movement on the 24th? Well, if Oli ji had not been there on the 24th, if such criminal activities and deeds had not happened, he might not have fled. I am not saying he fled. It is said that he has just moved places. Anyway, perhaps that would not have happened. But whoever committed criminal acts that day, this government is responsible for that day. I don't think so, and Gen Z should not take responsibility for the destruction and criminal deeds of the 24th, nor should this government. What do the facts say about these burnt structures? Honorable Chairman, this does not mean that there are no programs in this policy and program, that there are no correct programs. There are some things in it, such as completing business registration to construction permits within 30 days, investment express, establishment of Nepal Carbon Authority, Forest Research Center, high alert center. There is also a women's entrepreneurship strategy, e-gate system, payment gateway, remote work policy. And among them, what I find important is the concept of Nepal Origin Certified Water and branding Nepali products. Also, the provision that before the budget is passed, detailed project reports, environmental permits, and land acquisition will be mandatorily completed, procurement process will start from Shrawan, and the distortion of centralized expenditure in the month of Ashad will be ended by implementing zero-policy procurement. Also, there is an ambitious plan to produce 30,000 megawatts of electricity in the coming decade. Such things are not absent; they are present. Also, it is not that the declaration of the decade 2083/084 to 2092/093 as the Decade of Employment Promotion is not there, it is there. However, what does practice show? Practice shows that slum dwellers were driven away by bulldozers, terrorized by bulldozers, and their management has not been done even after the end of the fiscal year. Practice shows that our highest person, the President, has been insulted. The Honorable Prime Minister has insulted the place of the representatives of the people in a way that he has not addressed them so far. ... It shows that it has been done. Therefore, looking at these behaviors, these things do not seem likely to happen. Honorable Chairman, it has said nothing about the Nijgadh International Airport. This is a national pride project, such a significant airport, and it has said nothing about it. Therefore, it has not talked about the socialist-oriented national economy of Nepal as directed by the Constitution of Nepal, nor has it talked about the ambitious 7 percent economic growth rate, but it does not seem so. The possibility of that does not seem to exist. Therefore, policy on one side and behavior on the other, because of that, I do not see this policy and program being implemented. Therefore, I see the need to bring about extensive changes in this policy and program, introduce many amendments, and almost rewrite it. While presenting these points, I would like to conclude my views and suggestions on this policy and program. Thank you, greetings. Honorable Chairman: Honorable Member Somnath Poudel, time 5 minutes. (4:32 PM) Honorable Mr. Somnath Poudel (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairman, I would like to express my heartfelt thanks for the time. We are discussing the government's policy and program for 2083/084. The Prime Minister himself has boycotted the presentation of this policy and program, stating that it is directionless. The goals and objectives of the policy and program are like the human heart; if the heart is not beating, then having hands, feet, nose, and ears does not make sense, as I see it. Therefore, there are eyes, nose, ears, hands, and feet, but if the heart is not beating, it is like a living corpse. Therefore, I don't know what to say about this policy and program. There are two things that this government has omitted from its policy and program, looking at its behavior. One thing, I think, is that the government's first work started on the 12th of Baishakh. On the 12th of Baishakh, 2072, the Barpak earthquake destroyed the houses of about 8.5 lakh people. Exactly 13 years later, on the 12th of Baishakh, 2083, the Balen earthquake destroyed the houses of about 3,000 citizens. What kind of citizens' houses are to be destroyed? What is the policy for that? It would have been good if the government had brought it. How many poor citizens? How many citizens earning daily wages? How many citizens earning daily wages of 500, 700, 1000 rupees? Their houses are to be destroyed, that should have been brought, but it was not brought. I don't know why it was not brought. Let's just declare what was not brought. After all, now is the time to say "Wow" to whatever this government says. Bring it as a declaration. I don't see it coming in the program. While saying this, what did you do when you were in government? The question might arise. I want to remind the government that during the time of the government led by the then Chairman of the CPN-UML, KP Sharma Oli, due to the policies adopted at that time, about 8.5 lakh citizens' private houses damaged by the earthquake have been rebuilt. Today, those citizens are living in their homes. I want to remind you of this. I also want to remind you that on the 17th of Chaitra, 2075, in Bara-Parsa, a storm destroyed the houses of about 800 citizens, and within six months, the government handed over newly constructed houses to the citizens. I also want to remind you of that. We are seeing that this government has come not for construction, but for destruction, through its behavior. I want to remind you of a second thing. This government has arrested and killed Dalit community members in police custody. If you had brought a policy and program for that, it would have been good. You have promised in your manifesto, the government has promised in its manifesto, that we will announce special programs for Dalits within 10 days. But none of that has come in this policy and program. You are limited to making promises and deceiving the public. Therefore, in that context, I feel that this government has not brought any policy and program. I want to urge, keeping in mind that one swallow does not make a summer, I want to urge the government. In our Nepal, Bhutanese refugees, Tibetan refugees, and some other refugees have found shelter. But our own citizens are living their lives in refugee and hold centers.

Are they not citizens of Nepal? The government has no accountability towards those citizens. Announce who is to be evicted. I want to urge the government. Fourthly, is this policy program above the constitution? This policy program states that the right to form trade unions will be restricted. The constitution gives every citizen the right to organize. This cannot be violated. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I would like to inform you that the discussion on the policy and program of the Government of Nepal for the fiscal year 2083/084, mentioned in the address made by the Honorable President to a joint meeting of both houses of the federal parliament on Monday, Baishakh 28, 2083, could not be completed by the honorable members. Therefore, the discussion will continue in the next meeting. The next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Thursday, Baishakh 31, 2083, at 11:15 AM. This meeting is adjourned until then.
